mentions.name: Cangjie Workbook
mentions.description: This web app is a learning tool for Cangjie, a Chinese input method based on decomposing characters into sub-parts. It helps learners remember characters while typing, offers a free subset usable without login, and provides the complete product for a small monthly fee.
mentions.problem: Cangjie has a high learning curve, making it hard to pick up, though it is fun to type with and helps with remembering Chinese characters.
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on Cangjie Workbook. I am trying to create the best in class tool for learning Cangjie. It's a Chinese input method based on decomposing characters into sub parts (not necessarily related to how they are written).

mentions.name: Cangjie Workbook
mentions.description: This is a web-based course for learning Cangjie (倉頡), a Chinese input system based on the visual appearance of characters rather than etymology. The system lets users type most characters with unique output, avoiding the need to pick characters from a candidate list, which is especially useful when working with specialized Chinese texts. It includes a free demo and works on desktop and mobile web browsers.
mentions.problem: Typing Chinese characters typically requires selecting from a candidate list, which is inconvenient when working with specialized texts.
mentions.audience: People who work with specialized texts in Chinese.
mentions.source_excerpt: It's very niche, but I have created a course for learning Cangjie 倉頡, which is a Chinese input system based on the visual appearance of characters (not necessarily etymologically correct). The advantage of this system is you can type most characters via unique output (there are a few collisions where you need to pick) and you do not need to pick the character from a list.
